about: The Francoli family came from Campodolcino, a village high in the Italian Alps where logging and grappa-making were the main trades, and the family traces its distilling to 1875. In 1951 Luigi Francoli moved to Ghemme in northern Piedmont and rented a small, abandoned distillery; a few years later he and his four brothers bought their first still. Since 1964 the family has worked from a purpose-built distillery among the Ghemme vineyards, and its premium range carries Luigi’s name.

Antico Fernet Noveis takes its name from the Alpe di Noveis, the mountain pasture at whose foot its herbs are gathered. Many of the botanicals remain a family secret, but the known list includes gentian and gentianella, aloe ferox, mugwort, anise, quassia, mint, galangal, rhubarb root and white turmeric. It is naturally low in sugar and bottled at 40%.

In the glass it is jet black with a bold, bitter bite. Punch called it worth seeking out, but suggested sipping it neat or chilled over ice rather than swapping it one for one for Fernet-Branca in cocktails; if you do want a drink, a Toronto or an Eeyore’s Requiem shows off its depth and its long, drying bitterness.
